Here’s a structured 12-week hypertrophy plan tailored for a 26-year-old recreational lifter with full gym access, strict vegan diet, and a goal of building muscle while targeting 150 g protein/day from plants only. The program uses progressive overload, balanced volume, and evidence-based nutrition and recovery strategies.

Program overview
- Frequency: 4 lifting days/week (Upper/Lower split), optional 1 conditioning/mobility day
- Phases (3 x 4 weeks):
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation Hypertrophy + Technique
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive Overload + Intensification
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Advanced Hypertrophy + Strength Emphasis
- Progression: Double progression within rep ranges; add load when top of range is met for all sets
- Deload: Week 9 includes a volume/intensity taper to prime final push (see details)
- Session structure: 5–10 min warm-up, main lifts, accessories, finisher/conditioning (optional), cool-down
- RPE/RIR targets: Work sets around RPE 7–9 (1–3 reps in reserve), compounds slightly lower early in cycle

Key cues for vegan nutrition
- Protein target: 150 g/day entirely plant-based, ~1.8–2.0 g/kg for most women in this profile
- Calorie target: Start at maintenance + 200–300 kcal. Adjust +100–150 kcal if bodyweight not up ~0.25–0.5%/week by week 3.
- Protein distribution: 4–5 feedings/day, 25–40 g protein each, with 2–4 g leucine/meal (achievable via soy, pea blends, mycoprotein, seitan + legumes).
- Complementary proteins: Combine legumes + grains or use complete sources (soy, tofu/tempeh, edamame, soy milk, mycoprotein, pea/rice blends).
- Creatine: 3–5 g/day (vegan-friendly monohydrate). Vegan athletes tend to benefit more.
- Beta-alanine: 3.2–6.4 g/day divided; optional for higher-rep work.
- Omega-3 (EPA/DHA): 1–2 g/day from algae oil.
- Vitamin B12: 1000 mcg/week or 250 mcg/day.
- Vitamin D3 (vegan): 1000–2000 IU/day, adjust per labs.
- Iron: Monitor intake; consider 18 mg/day if labs/diet suggest low intake; pair with vitamin C.
- Calcium: Aim 1000 mg/day (fortified plant milks, tofu set with calcium sulfate, greens).
- Pre-workout: 20–40 g carbs + 20–30 g protein 60–90 min prior.
- Post-workout: 30–40 g protein (soy/pea blend) + 60–90 g carbs within 2 hours.

Weekly structure (example)
- Mon: Upper A
- Tue: Lower A
- Thu: Upper B
- Fri: Lower B
- Optional Sat: 20–30 min low-intensity cardio + mobility
- Wed/Sun: Rest

Warm-up and accessories
- Warm-up: 5 min light cardio + dynamic mobility (thoracic, hips, ankles, shoulders), 2–3 ramp-up sets per main lift.
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3 sec), strong concentric, full ROM.
- Rest: 90–150 sec on accessories, 2–3 min on compounds.
- Progression: When all sets at top reps with solid form, add 2–5% load next week.

Phase 1: Foundation Hypertrophy (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: Build volume tolerance, refine technique, establish mind–muscle connection. RPE ~7–8.

Week 1–2: (same exercises; week 2 aim +1 rep/set or small load bump if in range)

- Lat pulldown (wide or neutral): 3 x 10–12
- Incline DB fly or cable fly: 3 x 10–12
- Cable lateral raise: 3 x 12–15
- Cable triceps pressdown: 3 x 10–12

Optional finisher: Assault bike 6 x 15 s hard / 45 s easy (skip if recovery limited)

Lower A
- Back squat (high-bar): 4 x 6–8
- Romanian deadlift: 4 x 8–10
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8–10/side
- Leg press: 3 x 10–12
- Seated leg curl: 3 x 10–12
- Standing calf raise: 4 x 10–12

Upper B
- Incline DB bench press: 4 x 8–10

Week 3–4 adjustments
- Keep exercises; push toward top of rep ranges at same loads, then add 2.5–5 lb as able.
- Where noted 4 x 6–8, aim to reach 8s by week 4; accessories aim for 12–15s by week 4.
- If all top reps achieved, increase load modestly in week 4 and stay mid-range.

Phase 2: Progressive Overload (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Increase loads, slight drop in reps on key compounds; maintain or increase accessory volume. RPE 7.5–9.
